title: Irish crochet motif — the padded raised rose
subtitle: Work over a core pad of yarn to raise petals off the surface
excerpt: Irish crochet motifs are worked over a padding cord or core of spare yarn to raise the motif above the background mesh. The classic Irish rose is built from dc and tr petals worked in concentric rounds over this core. The padding cord is what gives Irish crochet its characteristic three-dimensional, sculptural quality.
sourceNotes: Therese de Dillmont, Encyclopedia of Needlework (1886), Project Gutenberg #20776 — padded raised crochet in Irish and Venetian guipure. Weldon's Practical Crochet, Vol. 7 (1892) — Irish crochet rose construction.

glossaryTerms.definition: A core of spare yarn threads laid across the work and worked over — stitches enclose the padding cord inside them. Used in Irish crochet to raise motifs, petals, and stems above the mesh background. The padding cord adds bulk without visible joins.
The open background mesh of Solomon's knots or chain-and-dc arches that holds Irish crochet motifs in place. Motifs are made separately and then tacked to the mesh, or the mesh is built around them.

attrs.title: Thread weight and hook size
attrs.body: Traditional Irish crochet uses cotton crochet thread (size 20-80) and a steel hook (0.75-1.5 mm). DK yarn on a 4 mm hook produces a much larger-scale training version — useful for learning the technique before moving to thread. All the method steps are identical regardless of scale.

content.text: Cut 8-10 strands of the same yarn as the padding cord, each about 15 cm. Hold them together as a bundle.
Ch 6. Sl st to first ch to make a ring. Fold the padding-cord bundle over the ring so it lies around the outside edge.
Round 1: dc into the ring — insert hook through the ring AND under the padding cord on each stitch. Work 10-12 dc over both the ring and the cord. Sl st to join.
Round 2 (first petal layer): *ch 3, skip 1 dc, sl st into next dc. Repeat from * around (5 or 6 petal loops).
Round 3: for each petal loop — (1 dc, 3 htr, 1 dc) into the ch-3 loop, working over the padding cord throughout.

Round 4 (second petal layer, behind round 2): sl st to back of round 1 stitches between petals. *Ch 5, sl st into next back-of-row position. Work (1 dc, 3 tr, 1 dc) into each ch-5 loop for larger petals behind the first row.

items.symptom: Padding cord shows through on the surface
items.cause: Working stitches loosely or using a padding cord thicker than the working yarn
items.fix: Keep stitches tight around the cord so it is fully enclosed. Use a padding cord the same weight or slightly thinner than the working yarn.

items.symptom: Petals don't stand up — they lie flat
items.cause: Not enough stitches in the petal shell, or too loose tension on the petal row
items.fix: Work at a tight tension. The petals curve and raise naturally when the stitch count is right — if they still lie flat, add one more stitch per petal to create more fullness.

content.text: Irish crochet leaves and stems are made using the same padding-cord technique over a straight chain or wire core. The mesh background that holds motifs together is a Solomon's knot grid or a ch-5-and-dc open mesh — both documented in the earlier stitch tutorials.
